summary.one_liner: Pygments is a generic syntax highlighter written in Python that supports over 500 languages and text formats.
summary.what_it_does: Pygments highlights source code and other text in many languages and formats, and is intended for use in code hosting, forums, wikis, or other applications that need to prettify code. The README describes it as supporting over 500 languages and text formats. It is installed with pip, either as the published Pygments package or in editable mode from a source checkout. The repository includes Sphinx documentation built with tox, with an optional demo page that requires Docker to build Pyodide. The README also covers development workflow (GitHub issues and pull requests, GitHub workflows for continuous testing) and a security note about execution time on untrusted input.
use_cases: highlight source code in a web page
add syntax coloring to a forum or wiki
render code in a code hosting site
convert source files to colored output
notable: Supports over 500 languages and text formats
Installable from PyPI with pip or as an editable checkout
Documentation includes an optional Pyodide-based demo page
Security section gives guidance on timeouts and concurrency limits for untrusted input
Tested with OSS-Fuzz and automated randomized testing
caveats: No execution-time guarantees; untrusted input may cause very long runs or high memory use
Building the demo page requires Docker
Some regular expressions can cause catastrophic backtracking, so processes should be time-limited
